title: 2020 HMMT November General Problem 7
statement: In triangle \(A B C\) with \(A B=8\) and \(A C=10\), the incenter \(I\) is reflected across side \(A B\) to point \(X\) and across side \(A C\) to point \(Y\). Given that segment \(X Y\) bisects \(A I\), compute \(B C^{2}\). (The incenter \(I\) is the center of the inscribed circle of triangle \(A B C\).)

solutions.text:
Define points as above and additionally let \(P\) and \(Q\) be the intersections of \(A I\) with \(E F\) and \(X Y\), respectively. Since \(I X=2 I E\) and \(I Y=2 I F, \triangle I E F \sim \triangle I X Y\) with ratio 2, implying that \(I P=\frac{1}{2} I Q=\frac{1}{4} I A\).
Let \(\theta=\angle E A I=\angle I E P\). Then \(\frac{I P}{I A}=\frac{I P}{I E} \frac{I E}{I A}=\sin ^{2} \theta\), implying that \(\sin \theta=1 / 2\) and \(\theta=30^{\circ}\). From here, proceed as in solution 1.
